Today we had a feast at Brick City Vegan!! #brickcityvegan Formerly known as Urban Vegan, this Newark- based fast-casual restaurant recently rebranded with a new name and updated menu. They have a variety of burgers including a housemade chickpea burger and housemade black eyed pea burger in addition to beyond meat. They also offer bowls with unique ingredients that you can’t get everywhere like bbq pulled oats, stewed black eyed peas, and black rice. 

Everything we had was super delicious, fresh, and made with clean ingredients. Pictured are a bowl with chickpeas, black rice, quinoa and veggies (probably my favorite thing), a black eyed pea burger, a California burger 🍔 with a Beyond Meat patty in it, biscuits, salad, and a chocolate chip cookie. I also had a lovely hibiscus tea 🌺 and Chris had a banana-strawberry smoothie. 
The staff was gracious and we really enjoyed our visit. So happy to have this spot in downtown Newark! 

📍 915 Broad Street across from Newark City Hall.

Another day, another ridiculous, nonsensical decision by Trump. This is the second time in a year Trump has moved to block Empire Wind 1—a crucial renewable energy project that links to the Sunset Park waterfront—and just like last time, there’s no coherent rationale.

This project has been thoroughly vetted and reviewed by multiple levels of government. To now claim a security threat, or whatever other excuse Trump is making up today, rings hollow. What this project does do is support thousands of good-paying jobs, ensure New Yorkers have reliable access to electricity, generate billions in investment in our neighborhoods, and strengthen our country's energy independence.

We fought Trump last time, and we’ll do so once again. Our future is on the line.

Kicking off my top 5 reads of 2025 in the 5th spot is Olga Dies Dreaming by Xochitl Gonzalez. 

Olga is such a strong and well written main character, the reader can’t help but start rooting for her right from the get go. She is a flawed MC, but one you would follow off a cliff if asked. The other characters, like her brother and the rest of her familia, have strong independent voices that make you wish you were invited to Sunday dinner. 

The writing is so impressive; sharp, engaging, and quick paced. I really appreciated the strong POC characters Gonzalez creates, in this book and others, and not shying away from tough important topics. As I said in my original review: if you are not a rich white man, odds are you will enjoy this novel!

December’s BAB (Big Apple Beautifiers 日本語は下にスクロール) marked our final cleanup in Brooklyn. Under a crisp, freezing-blue sky, we were able to expand our cleanup area thanks to a larger-than-expected turnout, and the day was filled with energy and smiles.

Looking back, six years ago we were forced to relocate because of COVID and began carving out new homes in Brooklyn, one step at a time.  Just when it felt like we had truly settled there, we were blessed with a reconnection to long-standing ties with former partners, almost as if in celebration of our upcoming 20th anniversary.  And so, starting in the new year, we will be returning to Manhattan.

Thank you for your dedication and enthusiasm! The cleanup event is truly a rewarding experience that leaves you feeling amazing and inspired. The Big Apple Beautifiers will meet every third Sunday at 9:00 AM at Hakata Tonton restaurant in Chinatown.  Our goal is to foster community spirit and enhance the beauty of our environment. Your unwavering support and love have been instrumental in the success of our 20-year-long monthly project. We deeply appreciate your involvement and look forward to many more years of collaboration!

It all started in 2019. We had a dream and a goal—to open a spot with the intention to truly provide an experience. But Covid hit and the world shut down. Over time trends have shifted, the mission has evolved and then came SAVŌ. Where hospitality meets Take Out. We’re not only here to provide the community with high quality, health conscious meals but also to educate with what should be common knowledge. Yesterday’s BATWorks meeting confirmed what we feared when our questions were tabled: a $100 million project on OUR waterfront is moving forward with decisions already made without meaningful community input.
What the community STILL doesn’t know:
❌ Who gets the space? Selection criteria unclear
❌ What does it cost? No pricing transparency for 7th & 8th floors
❌ Are Sunset Park residents prioritized? No guarantees
❌ How do we prevent displacement? No protections in place

The consortium led by LA’s LACI, operated by CIC (with a track record of accelerating gentrification), alongside NYU & CUNY is making moves on OUR waterfront while our community is kept in the dark.

This is not co-governance. This is not a Just Transition.
When outside entities decide what happens in Sunset Park without us at the table from day one, when “innovation spaces” come with price tags working families can’t afford, when workforce programs don’t prioritize the people who LIVE here—that’s extraction, not investment.

Sunset Park already has a plan - the GRID 2.0. Our community-led vision for a Just Transition. BATWorks must operationalize THE GRID, not replace it with outside agendas.
Sunset Park is not for sale.
We’ve been organizing for climate justice in this neighborhood since 1996. We know what real community leadership looks like.

What we demand:
BATWorks must align with and advance the GRID 2.0 community plan
Full transparency on cost models & tenant selection
Guaranteed prioritization for Sunset Park residents
Community oversight—not consultation AFTER decisions are made
Protection against displacement built into every contract
The clock is ticking. Sunset Park is watching. And we won’t be pushed out of decisions about OUR future.

following the october 30th flood, i completely disappeared from society for 4 weeks of intense isolation & cleaning. journeying through the stages of grief was incredibly painful, but i’m at a point where i believe the sun can & will rise again.  out of 2500 records or so, ultimately only 10% was lost. another 50 or 60% are damaged but playable. it will be months before this is fully behind me, but i want to publicly express how grateful i am for all the messages of love & support i received - i’m working on personally replying to them all💜

my records are my lifeblood; they are the story i want to tell. many have been with me longer than half my life. on wednesday december 17th, i will be playing some of my most meaningful discs that survived the flood at @bossanovacivicclub for my official birthday party - A Celebration Of Life . it’s not just my life, but the life of my records.  they still possess their magic, and this birthday party will center that magic in a very special way.

some good friends with their own magical records are on support, and there is of course no cover. this difficult event taught me that you don’t have to give up, but simply move on. it will always be inside of you.

In the cool limestone caves of Bouze-lès-Beaune, deep in Burgundy, Michel Couvreur pursued tradition. A Belgian by birth and Burgundian by conviction, he believed that Scotch whisky’s true soul lived not only in barley and peat, but in the wood itself. Beginning in the 1970s, he imported new-make spirit from Scotland, aging it patiently in ex-sherry casks drawn from Jerez bodegas, nurturing each barrel like a grand cru.

The result is a lineage of singular whiskies — luminous, oxidative, vinous — expressing the dialogue between Scotland’s distillate and France’s wine country. Each bottle carries his signature vision: that time, oak, and a bit of madness can turn spirit into poetry.

Chill out with a Manhattan this Independence Day.⁠
⁠
The Manhattan has been around forever: not quite as long as America, but it's getting up there! Its longevity can be attributed to the simple way in which the meltwater from the ice changes the flavor profile of the alcohol, much in the way wine responds to oxygen. Here's how to make it.⁠
⁠
2 oz Whiskey Row Bottled in Bond Bourbon⁠
1 oz Sweet Vermouth⁠
2 dashes Angostura Bitters⁠
⁠
Combine bourbon, sweet vermouth, and bitters in a mixing glass with ice. Stir until well chilled. Strain into a chilled coupe or rocks glass (serve on the rocks if preferred). Garnish with a brandied maraschino cherry or a twist of orange peel.⁠

You don't have to take our word for it. Jordan Hughes (@highproofpreacher) breaks down Whiskey Row Bourbon's three expressions:⁠
⁠
"Triple Wood 🥃 is their core expression, aged for at least 4 years and finished in Cognac and PX Sherry barrels. If you can get your hands on this bottle, do it! It’s a beautiful bourbon that harkens back to the early days of pre-Prohibition, when bourbon was all about experimentation. This one has a lot of depth and richness, and I love the enhanced fruit and spice notes from the Cognac barrels."⁠
⁠
"Bottled-in-Bond 🥃 I have a feeling this might become my go-to for cocktails. It adheres to the strict quality standards of the Bottled in Bond Act, including no additives, minimum 4-year aging under government supervision, and bottled at 100 proof, along with other regulations. That 100 proof is a real sweet spot for most bourbon cocktails, and I can already tell this bourbon will be a real star in some fun recipe concepts."⁠
⁠
"Cask Strength 🥃 is bold, unfiltered, and kinda in-your-face but in the best way. Whiskey Row’s Cask Strength is an incredibly robust but well-rounded bourbon with a ton of depth. If you want rich, complex flavor and a quality sipping experience, this is your jam—it’s certainly mine!"⁠
